info.title: Tools — smart-trust-tools
info.description: The call contracts of the harness's Tools, one operation per Tool, generated from the Tool nodes (`schemas/tools/tool.ts`) so standard API tooling can read them. **No HTTP server serves these paths**: each Tool is reached as its `x-invoke` says — a command line, an MCP tool, or an in-process call. Tags are the skills each Tool satisfies.

post.description: Write the viewer pages that site.build serves under viewers/: the graph explorer and traceability matrix over this instance's nodes (requirements, library sections, external schemas, references, directives, skills, Tools, processes, roles and beans), the requirements document, the WIT contract, the TypeScript reference (TypeDoc), the Kotlin skeleton and the wire and payload models. Also copies docs/*.md into the Jekyll source (site_docs.sh).

site.description: The built site; pages are written to <site>/viewers/.

x-selection.when: As the siteSteps of index.config.json's site.build recipe, when gh-pages is published by stage-local.
x-selection.limits: Reads the nodes as committed; does not validate them (check-req-nodes does).

post.summary: Check the vectors against the models
post.description: Decode the smart-trust PR 129 certificate and validate its payload against the CDDL (api/cddl and models/generated) and, through the JSON-LD context, the SHACL shapes.

report.description: One line per check; exit 1 on any failure.

x-selection.when: The CDDL, the derived models or a vector changed.
x-selection.limits: Checks the wire format and the payload shape only; the signature, the trust list and the time checks are hcert-core's tests.

post.description: Check every node of this instance's requirement graph: each skills/requirements/*.json parses as a bootstrap requirement with id req:<file>; every derivedFrom names a requirement and every reference a node that exists (a library section or entry, an external schema, a reference, a directive, a test vector, or a smart-trust FHIR Requirements canonical); every statement has a success criterion; every skill's satisfies and tested-by, every bean's requirements and sources, and every test plan resolve; every external schema and reference parses against its typology's schema; every code list parses as folio-code-list/v1, with every requirement's area a code of requirement-area; and the shared negative vectors parse against their schema, each expected step and reason a case of the WIT failure taxonomy.

report.description: One line per problem; exit 1 on any.

x-selection.when: Before the site is built (it is the recipe's pre step), and whenever a requirement, skill or bean is edited.
x-selection.limits: Checks references resolve, not that a quote matches its source.

post.summary: Check the upstream patches are well-formed
post.description: Check every file under upstream/ (the upstream-patches graph, kept on the state branch cat/smart-trust-tools/upstream-patches and mounted by state:mount): each is a numbered git format-patch file, upstream/<target>/NNNN-<subject>.patch, with the mbox From line, an author, a date, a [PATCH] subject, a --- separator and at least one diff --git hunk.

report.description: One line per problem; exit 1 on any, or when upstream/ is not mounted.

x-selection.when: A patch for an upstream repository was added or changed.
x-selection.limits: Checks the patch's form, not that it applies: that needs the upstream tree at the commit the patch was made against, so the maintainers' apply is that test.

post.summary: One TypeScript conformance suite for both libraries
post.description: suite.ts: 45 checks over every interface of the `hcert` world, type-checked (tsc, toolchain/node) against api/generated/ts, the TypeScript jco derives from the WIT contract, and driven by the shared vectors. run.mjs runs it against the Kotlin/JS package (hcert-core's WitJs facade) or the jco-transpiled Rust component; each loader only regroups its package's exports under the interface names. Both must pass (STT-TST-007). cross.mjs loads both and runs cross.ts: each library verifies the other's ES256 and PS256 certificates, built from byte-identical Sig_structures (STT-TST-003, STT-GEN-006).

dir.description: rust: the directory build-component.sh wrote; kotlin: hcert-core's build/compileSync/js/main/productionLibrary/kotlin.

report.description: One line per check; exit 1 on any failure.

x-selection.when: Either library or the WIT contract changed, or CI checks that the two implementations behave the same.
x-selection.limits: Runs on Node 22.18 or later (type stripping); the type check needs toolchain/node's tsc. Signs with node:crypto through the fixtures, so the suite itself has no Node types.
x-selection.cost: Seconds, once both libraries are built.

post.description: Fetch the DVCMin logical models as FHIR R5 StructureDefinitions from the smart-trust-phw build at the commit models/fhir/SOURCE.yaml pins, into models/fhir/.

x-selection.when: The pinned smart-trust-phw commit moved, and the logical models must be refreshed before lm-derive.
x-selection.limits: Fetches only the files SOURCE.yaml lists; never resolves a branch at run time.

post.description: Run the HL7 FHIR Validator (validator_cli.jar) on the StructureDefinitions in models/fhir against the FHIR version they declare, with the jar and every FHIR package pinned by sha256 in toolchain/fhir-validator/validator.json, verified before use, and no fetch at run time (-no-http-access, -tx n/a). The site's pre step: it runs when the site is published to main and says it is not run for a staging preview.

site.description: As the site's pre step: run only when SITE_BASEURL is the root's (main), not a STAGING preview's.

report.description: The validator's messages per StructureDefinition; exit 1 on an error, an unpinned artefact or a sha256 mismatch.

x-selection.when: The site is published to main, or a logical model in models/fhir changed and should be checked against FHIR itself.
x-selection.limits: Validates the StructureDefinitions as FHIR resources, without a terminology server; whether they map to the payload models is lm-derive's check. Refuses to run while any package validator.json lists has no sha256.
x-selection.cost: About a minute; the first run downloads the 200 MB jar and the packages into the cache.

post.summary: TypeScript declarations from the WIT contract
post.description: Run jco over api/wit to write the TypeScript view of the contract into api/generated/ts, the API reference that Node and browser callers read. jco comes from the pinned toolchain/node lockfile, installed with scripts disabled.

x-selection.when: api/wit changed, or CI re-generates the view and diffs it.
x-selection.limits: Types only: jco also validates the WIT package as it reads it, so a malformed contract fails here first.

post.description: The Kotlin implementation of the HCERT pipeline and Verifiable Health Links, for the JVM (Android as-is) and Node: `hcert-api`, the declarations wit2kotlin generates from the WIT contract, and `hcert-core`, the behaviour (deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256, ZLIB, Base45, HC1, the trust list, verification, the VHL payload, the ITI-YY5 manifest request and JWE dir/A256GCM). No third-party runtime dependency; every build artefact is pinned in gradle/verification-metadata.xml.

task.description: A Gradle task instead of `build`, for example `:hcert-core:jvmTest` or `:hcert-core:compileProductionLibraryKotlinJs`.

libraries.description: The JVM jars and the Kotlin/JS ES module under each module's build/.

x-selection.when: An application on the JVM, Android or Node issues, verifies or reads an HCERT, or shares or receives a VHL; or a change to the contract or the core is built and tested.
x-selection.limits: No QR rendering (the host renders the HC1 string), no HTTP (the host sends the ITI-YY5 request it builds), no key storage (the host signs the bytes prepare-sign returns). Rust (native and WebAssembly) is the second implementation, in tools/hcert-rust.
x-selection.cost: About a minute cold for the JVM and JS tests; Gradle downloads only artefacts the verification metadata lists.

post.description: The Rust implementation of the HCERT pipeline: Base45, ZLIB, deterministic CBOR, COSE_Sign1 ES256/PS256 (RustCrypto p256, rsa, sha2), CWT, the DVCMin payload, the trust store (PEM, DER, GDHCN DID trustlist v2, trust domains), the section 11 verifier, two-phase issuance and Verifiable Health Links (payload, vhlink:/, the ITI-YY5 manifest, JWE dir/A256GCM with aes-gcm, the RFC 9421 signature base). It builds natively; as the WebAssembly component of the `hcert` world in api/wit (feature component, wit-bindgen; build-component.sh componentises and transpiles it with the pinned jco into an ES module for browsers and Node, whose only import, wasi:random, maps to crypto.getRandomValues); and as an import-free module with a JSON call surface for the live demos (js/hcert.mjs, with a TEST ONLY builder of self-signed DSCs). Every crate is pinned in Cargo.lock (DEPENDENCIES.md).

target.description: wasm32-unknown-unknown for the WebAssembly module (with `cargo build --release`), else the host.

library.description: tools/hcert-rust/target/<target>/release/: the rlib, and hcert.wasm for wasm32.

x-selection.when: A Rust program or a web page issues or verifies an HCERT, or a demo shows the QR Code Generation steps live; or the second implementation is checked against the first on the shared vectors.
x-selection.limits: No coverage-guided fuzzing in CI (cargo-fuzz needs nightly); the seeded fuzzer runs instead. The codec does not yet build without std. Not yet published to crates.io or npm (STT-NFR-002); the crate (cargo package) and the npm component package (tools/release-packaging) are ready, for an agent to publish by docs/RELEASING.md.
x-selection.cost: Seconds once the crates are cached; the first build downloads the crates Cargo.lock pins (72 for the library, 29 more for the component).

post.summary: Payload models from the FHIR logical models
post.description: Derive, from the FHIR logical models in models/fhir, the JSON-LD context, SHACL shapes and CDDL rules in models/generated/ that the payload codecs and the conformance checks read.

check.description: Write nothing; fail if a generated file is stale.

x-selection.when: A logical model changed, or CI checks the derived models are current.
x-selection.limits: Maps kind=logical FHIR 5.0.0 models: direct elements of a FHIR primitive or model type, cardinality, bindings, codes, and "a.exists() or b.exists()" invariants. Anything else (a nested element, another type, a choice, a profile, an element invariant, another expression) is an error naming the model and element, in both modes, unless tools/lm-derive/allow-unmapped.json excuses it with a reason.

post.description: Derive vectors/negative/negative-vectors.json from the smart-trust PR 129 certificates: one language-neutral file of inputs a conforming verifier must refuse, each with the step and reason it must stop at. The Kotlin suite, the Node smoke test and the Rust suite load the same file. Nothing is newly signed: each case changes a byte, a prefix, the clock or the trust list.

check.description: Write nothing; fail if the file is stale.

x-selection.when: A negative case is added, or the PR 129 vector changes.
x-selection.limits: Covers the steps reachable without a new signature; a case needing a new signer (a key usage mismatch, a missing hcert claim) stays in the Kotlin tests' testkit.

post.description: Assemble the two npm packages of the libraries, @litlfred/hcert-component (the jco-transpiled Rust component) and @litlfred/hcert-kotlin-js (the Kotlin/JS library), from their build outputs, each with a package.json that has the VERSION, no dependencies and no scripts; and check that VERSION, the single version source, is a semantic version that Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, the Gradle build, CHANGELOG.md and every built package.json and POM agree with. The Maven dry run is the hcert-kotlin build's publishDryRun task and the crate's is cargo package; docs/RELEASING.md is the runbook an agent follows to publish.

artefacts.description: A directory of built artefacts (the npm dist directory, the Maven dry-run repository) whose package.json and .pom versions are checked too.

packages.description: With assemble-npm.mjs --out <dist>: <dist>/hcert-component and <dist>/hcert-kotlin-js, ready for npm pack.

x-selection.when: Before a release, or in CI: the version must agree everywhere and every artefact must package, without publishing.
x-selection.limits: Publishes nothing and holds no credentials: an agent publishes by docs/RELEASING.md, never a workflow. No Android AAR (the JVM jar serves Android until an androidTarget exists). The crate leaves out the tests, which read ../../vectors, and its `component` feature, which reads ../../api/wit, builds only from the repository.
x-selection.cost: Milliseconds, once the libraries are built.

post.summary: Every test has a Gherkin Scenario
post.description: Check test/features/*.feature against the suites: every Rust #[test], Kotlin @Test and TypeScript conformance run(...) has a Scenario tagged @test:<path>::<test>, every such tag names a test, WHO-ITB Scenarios carry @itb:<suite>/<testcase>, and every test-plan case names its feature file. Temporary, until cat-harness check:test-gherkin is pinned.

list.description: Print each test's @test: tag and check nothing.

200.description: The Tool declares no typed output.

x-selection.when: A test or a feature file is added, renamed or removed, or CI checks they agree.
x-selection.limits: Checks the tags, not that the steps match the test's assertions: a reviewer reads that.

post.description: Write test/plans/hcert-library-conformance.test-plan.json (test-plan/v1) from the skills and the requirements' success criteria: one case per skill, one assertion per criterion verified by test. The plan any implementation of the library, Kotlin or Rust, runs.

check.description: Write nothing; fail if the plan is stale.

x-selection.when: A requirement's success criteria or a skill's satisfies changed, or CI checks the plan is current.
x-selection.limits: Writes the library plan only; who-itb-agreement is authored by hand.

post.summary: Systems under test and their bindings
post.description: Write the bindings and uncovered lists of each test/systems/<id>.system.json (system/v1) from the tags in its tests: the requirement ids a Kotlin, Rust or TypeScript test's name starts with, or a script's "Verifies" sentence. Each assertion of a plan the system claims gets the tests that verify it, with the surface and target each runs on; each required assertion a declared target leaves unverified, and no `unbound` entry explains, is listed as uncovered.

check.description: Write nothing; fail if a system file is stale or a tag names no requirement or criterion.

systems.description: test/systems/*.system.json, with bindings and uncovered rewritten.

x-selection.when: A test is added or renamed, a suite moves, a requirement's success criteria change, or CI checks the systems are current.
x-selection.limits: Reads tags, not results: a binding says which test verifies an assertion, not that it passed. A run records the verdict.

post.description: Make vectors/ihe-vhl/jwe-dir-a256gcm.json with node:crypto alone, so the library's RFC 7516 dir / A256GCM decryption (with and without zip DEF) is checked against an implementation that is not the library. TEST ONLY: the key is in the file.

x-selection.when: The JWE fixture is lost or its format must change.
x-selection.limits: Random each run: the committed file is the vector, and re-running replaces it.

post.summary: Kotlin skeleton from the WIT contract
post.description: Generate the Kotlin declarations in tools/hcert-kotlin/hcert-api from api/wit by fixed mapping rules: records to data classes, variants to sealed interfaces, resources to AutoCloseable interfaces, result<T, E> to HcertResult; worlds are not generated, and no Kotlin name or KDoc mentions WIT.

check.description: Write nothing; fail if a generated file is stale.

x-selection.when: api/wit changed, or CI checks the Kotlin skeleton is current.
x-selection.limits: Reads the subset of WIT this contract uses; an unsupported construct is an error, not a guess. Writes declarations only, never behaviour.

Flag.description: A boolean switch — projects to a bare flag, with no value word

RepoPath.description: A path relative to the repository root. No `..` segments.

Text.description: A short single-line human string. Not admissible as a command-line argument.
